main_text.head: QUIS EST TERTIUS Titulus?
De servitutibus praediorum. Von dienstbarkeiten der liegenden güter.
main_text.p: Duplex : personalis aut realis. Personalis, quae à persona personae debetur, ut est in hominibus servilis conditionis, de qua supra dictum est: vel quae à persona rei debetur, ut quando persona cogitur certo cuidam loco assistere: Realis est, quae à re, rei debetur.
Duplex: Rustica aut urbana Rustica, quae rusticis praediis debetur: Urbana, q̄ urbanis prędiis debetur.
Rustica prędia dicuntur ipsi agri vel fundi. Item ędificia, quae sunt structa[?] pro rebus rusticis, pecoribus & fructibus, sive sint in urbe, sive extra urbem.
Urbana prędia dicuntur ędificia, inhabitādi gratia facta, & hominum usui & habitationi destinata, sive in urbe, sive extra urbem in rure vel villa posita sint. Vide Schneidevvinum.

Ad hoc autem ut cognoscatur an sit servitus rustica seu urbana, inspicitur qualitas prędii dominantis, cui servitus debetur: non prędii servientis, quod servitutem debet. Unde licet via sit servitus rustica, tamen si debetur pe fundum tuum domui meae, dicitur urbana servitus, secundum Schneidevvinum.

l.bl: Iter, der fußpfad. Actus, der treibe weg. Via, der fahrweg.

page.notes: The title "QUIS EST TERTIUS" is printed large and spaced; the caput number is inferred from the word "Tertius". The German headings and gloss words are in blackletter. Line 1 of the first paragraph opens with a large D, joined to the text as "Duplex". In "Q̄ urbanis" the abbreviation mark is read as q̄ and may be doubtful. "structa" is partly obscured by ink and marked [?]. "Schneidevvinum" is printed as shown and is a printing spelling, left as is. "pe fundum" is printed so and left as is.
